items.title: Proposition 3.61 · ambient-to-tangent gradient projection

source.anchor: §3.8, Definition3.58 and equations3.36–3.38; Proposition3.61 (3.39), printed42–44 / PDF58–60
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. Samplinglib attributed restatement; library prerequisite is explicitly narrower in geometry and broader in pointwise regularity.

items.statement: On a Riemannian submanifold of Euclidean space with the induced metric, the gradient of a smooth function is the tangent-space orthogonal projection of the ambient gradient of any smooth neighborhood extension.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean ambient space and embedded submanifold with induced Riemannian metric.
Smooth real-valued f on the manifold and a smooth extension to a neighborhood.

obligations.label: Canonical gradient under linear/affine restriction with inherited metric.
Actual nonlinear tangent/differential and extension-independence adapter.
Smoothness of the resulting manifold gradient field.

bindings.boundary: This is the linear/affine restriction prerequisite for Boumal §3.8. Arbitrary embedded-manifold tangent identification, differential restriction, extension semantics and smooth gradient fields remain open; Proposition 3.61 and Chapter 3 are not complete.

assumption_deltas.source: Finite Euclidean ambient and tangent subspaces.
assumption_deltas.lean: Complete real Hilbert E and complete linear subspace K.
assumption_deltas.reason: The pairing mechanism works for complete subspaces; finite-dimensional source instances satisfy completeness. This is not a nonlinear tangent adapter.

assumption_deltas.source: Smooth function and smooth neighborhood extension.
assumption_deltas.lean: Pointwise genuine HasGradientAt for f:E→ℝ; literal affine restriction.
assumption_deltas.reason: One-point differentiability suffices for this library node. The source requires independent nonlinear extension/differential semantics.

assumption_deltas.lean: Inherited inner product on K and gradient typed in K.
assumption_deltas.reason: The chosen subspace metric is exactly inherited. No arbitrary Riemannian metric identification is claimed.
